overview: Two structural boundaries of the cell: one rigid and optional, one flexible and universal to all cells.
genZNote: Membrane: every cell's ID badge. Wall: the bonus armor some cells get.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A rigid outer layer found in plants, fungi, and most bacteria/archaea, providing structural support and protection.
aspects.valueB: The universal phospholipid bilayer surrounding every cell, regulating what enters and exits.

aspects.label: Presence Across Life
aspects.valueA: Present in plants, fungi, algae, and most bacteria/archaea — absent in animal cells.
aspects.valueB: Present in every living cell without exception.

aspects.label: Composition
aspects.valueA: Cellulose (plants), chitin (fungi), or peptidoglycan (most bacteria), depending on the organism.
aspects.valueB: Phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins, cholesterol (in animals), and glycolipids/glycoproteins.

aspects.label: Permeability
aspects.valueA: Generally freely permeable to water and small solutes — it is a structural, not a selective, barrier.
aspects.valueB: Selectively permeable — controls transport via channels, carriers, and pumps.

aspects.label: Rigidity
aspects.valueA: Rigid, providing shape and protection against osmotic lysis.
aspects.valueB: Fluid and flexible (fluid mosaic model), allowing movement of embedded proteins.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Rigid, protective, only in some organisms.
aspects.valueB: Flexible, selectively permeable, universal to all cells.
